headline: Rocks are Earth's autobiography—every layer records ancient worlds
universal_truth: The past is preserved all around us, waiting to be read
fun_facts: Some rocks contain fossils of creatures that lived over 3 billion years ago
The Grand Canyon's layers span 2 billion years of Earth's history
Geologists can read climate, extinctions, and even asteroid impacts in rock layers
discussion_questions: What 'layers' have you accumulated that tell your story?
How does reading Earth's past help us understand our present?
What story will our layer tell future geologists?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Pick up a rock and you're holding a time capsule. That ordinary stone might contain a record of ancient seas, vanished creatures, or climate shifts from before dinosaurs existed. Rocks are Earth's autobiography—layer after layer of history, waiting to be read.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: How do scientists read the past in stone? How can a rock reveal what lived, what the climate was, even whether an asteroid struck—millions of years ago? What secrets are encoded in the layers?
cliff.prompt: How do rocks record Earth's history?

options.text: Sediments bury and preserve fossils, minerals, and chemical signatures over time
options.response: Yes. Each layer of sediment is a snapshot of its time—preserved under the weight of ages.

options.text: Radioactive elements in rocks decay at known rates, revealing age
options.response: Radiometric dating tells age, but layers tell the story...

q1.title: Layer by Layer
q1.script: Sedimentary rocks form in layers—each layer deposited in a different time. The deeper the layer, the older the rock. The Grand Canyon is a 2-billion-year timeline carved into visible strata. Walk from rim to river and you walk backward in time.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Layer by Layer"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Fossil Libraries
q2.script: Fossils are life's autobiography embedded in stone. From microscopic bacteria to dinosaur skeletons, rocks preserve what lived. The sudden disappearance of species in rock layers marks mass extinctions. Rocks record both life and death.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Chemical Memories
q3.script: Rocks record more than fossils. Certain chemical signatures reveal ancient oxygen levels, temperatures, and even asteroid impacts. A thin layer of iridium worldwide marks the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs. Earth remembers everything.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The past is preserved all around us. Rocks remind us that everything leaves a record—and that with patience and attention, we can read stories written in the most unlikely places.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 67. Tomorrow, we'll explore Earth's hidden treasures—minerals and gems. Until then, pick up a rock and wonder: what story is it telling?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Reading Layers - Find Your Story in History
growTrack.learning_objective: See how layers of experience create personal history
growTrack.activity: Your life has layers too. Identify three 'layers' in your personal history—distinct periods that shaped who you are. What does each layer contain? What transitions between layers? Your story is readable in your accumulated experiences.
